design_rationale:
STEP 0 SNAPSHOT (task 0 of 2, claimed first): no prior tasks exist yet; this task claims the difficulty's single workflow plus the root problem it terminates in. Occupied after this task: corp_ext_dues_billing, corp_ext_payment_allocation, corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver, the workflow corp_wf_new_enrollment_onboarding, and tools activate_corp_enrollment_8f54bf3c / bill_corp_enrollment_dues_4e718c02 / record_corp_dues_payment_5148c010 / waive_corp_wellness_reimbursement_b40ef430. ROUND (KB-BIJECTION/KB-RUNTIME rework): the three policies' rule text now states explicitly that the employee's own club membership monthly_dues_usd rate is the amount of that membership's own most recent recurring-dues charge on file -- this was always true of this task's seed (Priya's membership_events already carries a recent $29.99 recurring_dues charge), but the resolution path was previously undocumented in the policy text itself, which a difficulty-wide KB-bijection audit flagged as a domain-wide gap (present regardless of any one task's seed). No seed or GT value changed for this task. Remaining headroom for task 1: corp_billing_and_suspension's late-fee/suspension machinery and reinstatement, none of which this task touches (this task's enrollment is never suspended), so task 1 has an independent, load-bearing chain of its own (late fee -> missed-payment recovery -> reinstatement fee), pairwise disjoint from this task's tools and policies.

WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST: the surface goal ('finish activating my enrollment and apply my employer's wellness reimbursement') never names amount_usd for any of the three writes; the agent must read corp_tier_pricing/corp_ext_dues_billing to learn the first-cycle setup-fee branch, read corp_ext_payment_allocation to learn a payment cannot post before a bill exists, and read corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver to learn the waiver is capped by BOTH an annual reimbursement cap AND 3x trailing payments -- none of which the caller states or hints. Difficulty is long (activate -> bill -> pay -> waive, 4 steps, no step reorderable) and broad (tier params, a cross-category CPARAM read of the employee's own membership dues, two independent history sums (ytd_waived, ytd_paid), and a first-bill branch keyed off a COUNT of this enrollment's own billing history).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD: corp_enrollment_verification -- satisfied by the enrollment record itself once its status shows active (this task's own step is the evidence, per base's own rule: 'the enrollment record itself, once its status shows active, is the system evidence that this verification was completed'), with the caller's verbal statement that she has a recent paystub on hand satisfying the immediate, current_user_input side of that check. corp_dues_waiver_policy (status active or suspended for corp_dues_waived; also referenced for corp_dues_payment_received under policy_scope) -- satisfied because by the time the payment and the waiver are posted, the activation step has already moved the enrollment to active. corp_agg_multi_holding / corp_membership_bundling_requirement / corp_re_enrollment_cooldown / corp_employer_size_tier_gate / corp_guest_pass_allotment all govern corp_enrollment_created, which this task never writes (the enrollment already exists at frozen_time in the applied state, submitted through another channel before this call), so none of them is a base_precondition of any write this task's GT performs.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: the target object is Priya's own corporate wellness enrollment (enrollment_id=a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-a0b1-c2d3e4f56789), customer_id=575df187-9295-477b-aa25-9747667291ed, employer_account_id=EMP-4471-SB. No reversal, compensation or adjustment row exists for this enrollment since it has no billing history yet; every SUM/COUNT primitive in corp_ext_dues_billing / corp_ext_payment_allocation / corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver auto-scopes to enrollment_id=HID, so no other employee's billing history could ever leak in.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD (revised round 2, per source-layer audit finding SOURCE-CHAIN RED on the prior Edge 1 = waiver->dues_billing state_gate/prior_bills_exist: that edge was decorative -- corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver's compute never read a prior_bills_exist/COUNT(corp_dues_billed) binding, and its entire practical effect was already, independently produced by the sibling value_input edge below via the payment_ceiling chain, so the edge has been removed from both the policy YAML and this closure rather than kept as a non-load-bearing decoration; the rule's own opening sentence asserting that gate was removed in the same pass so rule and compute no longer diverge): root_problem = corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver (the caller's second, compound ask: 'and can you also get my employer's wellness reimbursement applied'). Edge 1: waiver -> corp_ext_payment_allocation, kind=value_input, gate=payment_ceiling. Condition/policy_source (quoted from corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver's own rule): 'The amount waived may also never exceed 3 times the total payments the employer's master account has made toward this enrollment in the trailing 12 months ending at the time of the waiver.' Unresolved at frozen_time because the enrollment itself does not exist yet at the opening (still status=applied, with no billing or payment history at all). Resolved by record_corp_dues_payment_5148c010; once that lands, payment_ceiling = 3 * 20.50 = 61.50. Edge 2 (payment_allocation -> dues_billing, kind=value_input, gate=current_balance): payment cannot post before a bill exists (F('corporate_dues_balance') is 0.00 until the bill lands); resolved by bill_corp_enrollment_dues_4e718c02. Topological order: corp_ext_dues_billing -> corp_ext_payment_allocation -> corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver -- a strict total order (not a free parallel choice) because payment_allocation is itself a prerequisite of the waiver AND is itself downstream of dues_billing, so no other order avoids both gates being unmet. DELETION SENSITIVITY: skipping corp_ext_dues_billing's write leaves corporate_dues_balance at 0.00 so payment_allocation's own result becomes 0.00 (MN(MX(0,0),1499.50)=0.00) instead of 20.50, and the waiver's payment_ceiling becomes MN(candidate,cap_headroom,0.00)=0.00 instead of 7.50 -- both remaining edges are load-bearing; both are kind=value_input, satisfying the '>=1 value_input edge' requirement twice over. user_scenario never names corp_dues_billed, corp_dues_payment_received, a 'first bill', a 'setup fee' or a payment amount; the caller only ever expresses the compound surface goal of finishing her activation and getting the reimbursement applied. The tool layer validates nothing: bill_corp_enrollment_dues_4e718c02, record_corp_dues_payment_5148c010 and waive_corp_wellness_reimbursement_b40ef430 all simply write their given amount_usd with no precondition check in task_tools.py (each only checks that the enrollment_id row exists, never a policy precondition).

ZERO-WAIT CAUSAL CARD (workflow corp_wf_new_enrollment_onboarding): step 0 (activate_corp_enrollment_8f54bf3c, owner=agent) -- every prerequisite is initial_state_preexisting (the enrollment already exists, status=applied) plus current_user_input (the caller confirms she has her paystub in hand, satisfying corp_enrollment_verification's evidence requirement immediately, same turn). Step 1 (bill_corp_enrollment_dues_4e718c02) -- prerequisite is prior_synchronous_tool_effect: step 0's real status flip to active. Step 2 (record_corp_dues_payment_5148c010, owner=user) -- prerequisite is prior_synchronous_tool_effect: step 1's real corporate_dues_balance increase to 20.50, plus current_user_input (the caller, authorized to act for the employer's billing, confirms and posts the payment herself once handed the tool). Step 3 (waive_corp_wellness_reimbursement_b40ef430) -- prerequisite is prior_synchronous_tool_effect: step 2's payment (for payment_ceiling), which itself required step 1's bill (for current_balance). No step ever waits on a diagnosis, delivery, external approval, back-office batch or the passage of real time; every fact consumed was either true at the opening or produced synchronously by an earlier step in this same call.

STANDARD SOLUTION / STEP 5 VERIFICATION: locate Priya via find_customers, verify identity (phone_number + date_of_birth, 2 matches), read her membership holding (Base Club Access, active, monthly_dues_usd=29.99 via the tier's own catalogue value), read her membership billing history (reconciles to dues_balance=0.00), and find her existing corporate enrollment (status=applied). Activate it. Read corporate_wellness_events for that enrollment_id (empty) to confirm prior_bills_count=0 -> is_first_bill=True; setup_fee_raw=RND(0.05*29.99,2)=1.50, MN(1.50,5.00)=1.50 (the $5 cap does NOT bind -- the untriggered branch); bill amount_usd = RND(19.00+1.50,2)=20.50. Hand over the payment tool for Priya to post: current_balance=20.50, ceiling=50*29.99=1499.50 (does NOT bind -- second untriggered branch), amount_usd=MN(20.50,1499.50)=20.50, balance -> 0.00. Waive the reimbursement: pct=25, annual_cap=100.00, candidate=RND(0.25*29.99,2)=7.50, ytd_waived=0.00 (no prior waiver history) so cap_headroom=100.00 (does not bind), ytd_paid=20.50 so payment_ceiling=RND(3*20.50,2)=61.50 (does not bind), amount_usd=MN(7.50,100.00,61.50)=7.50. This was executed with the actual compute expressions above and matches computations[].expected exactly.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT ONLY (masking compute/expected/GT): reading only the published rule prose, the tool docstrings, and the caller's own words, a rollout would (1) locate and verify the caller, (2) find her applied enrollment and discover from corp_enrollment_verification's text that activation follows once employment is confirmed, (3) discover from corp_ext_dues_billing's rendered rule that the first bill includes a capped, membership-dues-linked setup fee and compute it from the membership holding's own tier parameter, (4) discover from corp_ext_payment_allocation's rendered rule that a payment requires an existing bill, that it is the employee's own action to confirm on the employer's behalf, and apply it in full up to the balance, (5) discover from corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver's rendered rule that a waiver is capped by both the annual cap and 3x trailing payments (zero until a payment has posted), and compute the same 7.50. This converges on the identical write sequence, objects and parameters as gold above with no second reasonable reading.
user_scenario: Priya Nandakumar calls in sounding upbeat and a little rushed -- she is on her lunch break. "Hi, this is Priya Nandakumar -- I applied online last week for the corporate wellness thing through Fernwood Analytics, and HR said it should be ready to activate, so I wanted to get that finished on my account today if you can do it for me." If asked to confirm she wants the representative to handle it on her behalf rather than her doing it herself, she says yes, that is exactly what she is hoping for -- "if you can do it for me" is basically her whole reason for calling. If asked how to verify her, she gives her phone number, "2125550410", and if a second detail is needed she gives her date of birth, reading it off her own file as "1989-04-12"; if pressed for a photo id, she mentions her driver license number is "DL-W4012345", of which the last four digits are "2345". She already has her regular club membership -- she has been a member downtown for a couple of years -- and is not calling about that today. When asked to confirm her employer, she says the company is "Fernwood Analytics", and when asked for the plan name, she says HR called it the "Small Business Partner" plan. If asked whether she has any proof of employment handy, she says "I have a recent paystub pulled up on my phone right now" and can read off whatever is needed from it. Once the representative tells her the enrollment is active, she adds: "Oh, one more thing -- HR also mentioned the wellness partnership reimburses part of my gym dues every so often. Can you get that applied for me too while we're at it?" She does not know how much that comes to or how it is calculated -- she is just repeating what HR told her. If the representative explains that the first billing cycle needs to be charged and paid before anything else can be figured, she says that is fine, go ahead -- their office handles the corporate billing centrally, so she is glad to confirm and post that payment herself right now if that is how it works on your end. Once the representative tells her the reimbursement has been applied, she thanks them and says that's everything she needed today.
